name: CEARCH: exploratory cause-prioritisation research (Ambitious Impact, 2021 idea report)
summary: Ambitious Impact's 2021 estimate for a new charity doing exploratory cause-prioritisation research, to find and promote new cause areas and interventions for effective altruist and other donors. The idea CEARCH (the Centre for Exploratory Altruism Research) was founded to run in 2022. A re-implementation of AIM's spreadsheet, traced from its five-year benefit-cost ratio, in dollars of current effective-altruist donations' worth of value per dollar spent; our bridge values those dollars like the donations they stand for. Ambitious Impact notes that 'this CEA is only comparable to other CEAs created for EA meta charities by Charity Entrepreneurship'.

source.title: EA Meta: Exploratory Altruism (CE 2021 top idea report): CEA

rows.explainer: Costs start at $150,000 and grow 20% a year: $150,000 × (1.2⁵ − 1) / 0.2 = $1,116,240 over five years. The sheet caps growth after 8 years, which doesn't bind at 5.

rows.label: Average cost per year
Benefit-cost ratio over the years modelled
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact's bottom line: value created over five years, in dollars of today's top-tier effective-altruist donations, per dollar spent. The report gives the third year as an example, 'Leverage ratio ~8'. The sheet's note (CEA!F17:J17) places it between a fundraising organisation's money moved per dollar (4:1) and a successful think tank's (10:1 or more), with no source for either.

rows.label: Value of benefits that come a year after the costs
rows.explainer: The sheet's benefits start a year after its costs (its 'impact delayed by 1 year') and both are summed undiscounted. We discount the benefits by that lag at the shared discount rate (Your values); the evaluator view pins it to 0, as the sheet has it.

rows.label: Method 2's lasting impact, discounted for time as well
rows.formula: 1 - method2_impact_used * method2_weight / (method1_impact_used * method1_weight + method2_impact_used * method2_weight) * (1 - idea1_replaceability / (idea1_replaceability + $discount_rate))
rows.explainer: Method 2 values each idea's yearly impact as a perpetuity that shrinks by 15% a year, the chance someone else would do the work later (the same 15% for all three ideas): yearly impact ÷ 0.15. Time preference would shrink it further, to yearly impact ÷ (0.15 + the discount rate). This applies that to method 2's share of the weighted impact (about 55%); method 1 is unaffected. At the evaluator view's 0% it is 1.

rows.label: Chance the new organisation succeeds

source.title: Ambitious Impact, Better Futures Guide CEA (2025): probability of success from AIM's incubated charities

rows.explainer: The sheet assumes the organisation succeeds ('did not discount for chance of organizational failure', CEA!D61), because its comparison organisations (ACE, GiveWell, Rethink Priorities) are ones that succeeded. Ambitious Impact's own later estimate for a new research and advice charity, from how its incubated charities fared, is about 56%. Our judgment 60%, range 40–80% (ours); the evaluator view uses the sheet's 100%. This overlaps partly with method 2, whose ideas already carry a yearly chance of success (2.5–40%): that is the chance an idea finds traction, this is the chance the organisation lasts to pursue it, so we apply it to both methods.

rows.explainer: The donations whose direction CEARCH's research changes, per dollar CEARCH spends, weighted like Ambitious Impact's two methods: the money comparable organisations moved, and the money each of the three ideas moves over the years with impact. With credit by share of resources on, those donors paid for the good their gifts do, so they share the outcome with CEARCH's budget and staff.

rows.label: Share of the outcome credited to CEARCH's cash budget
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, everyone who paid for the outcome shares it: CEARCH's budget, staff's forgone pay, and the donors whose gifts its research redirects. Off, this is 100%.

source.title: GiveWell, cost-effectiveness models (updated September 2026)
source.quote: The previous benchmark was based on GiveDirectly's flagship unconditional cash transfers program.
source.note: 0.00335 units of value per dollar is the benchmark's value in GiveWell's sheets, the same figure the GiveWell imports use.

rows.explainer: GiveWell's benchmark: its older estimate of the good a dollar given to GiveDirectly does, 0.00335 units of value. GiveWell's funding bars are multiples of it. (GiveWell now thinks GiveDirectly itself is three to four times better than this old estimate; the benchmark is still the unit the bars are stated in.)

rows.label: Value of a dollar of top-tier EA donations, in multiples of GiveWell's benchmark

source.title: GiveWell blog, We aim to cost-effectively direct around $1 billion annually by 2025 (November 2021); GiveWell, cost-effectiveness models (2026)
source.quote: This year, we expect to identify $400 million in 8x or better opportunities. (2021) / As of May 2026, our bar for funding programs is 6x our benchmark. (2026)

rows.explainer: CEARCH's value reaches people through the charities the money it influences goes to. Ambitious Impact counts the value in 'equivalent donations to today's current top-tier EA charities', and warns that 'this CEA is only comparable to other CEAs created for EA meta charities by Charity Entrepreneurship'. To put such dollars on the site's scale we value them like donations to GiveWell's top charities at the time of Ambitious Impact's 2021 report: GiveWell then funded opportunities at '8x or better' its benchmark, so the best guess is 8 (its bar is 6 today). Low end 2: part of top-tier EA money goes to animal welfare and longtermist work, which has no agreed value on this scale, so we allow for these dollars being worth much less here than GiveWell's bar. High end 15: GiveWell's current model of the Against Malaria Foundation, as imported on this site, comes to about 0.049 units of value per dollar, 15 times the benchmark. The bridge and its range are ours, not Ambitious Impact's.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar you give
rows.explainer: Dollars of EA-donation value per dollar, valued like donations to GiveWell's top charities, in GiveWell's units of value. The headline turns units of value into healthy years at the shared rate.
